title: How to Verify OSINT Account Matches | MyRecon
description: Verify username leads with original URLs, independent public links, conflicts and an illustrative decision log. Keep unresolved matches explicit.
intro: A username match answers whether a page may exist under a handle. It does not answer who controls the page. Use this decision process to distinguish a candidate, a corroborated public link and a claim you cannot support. It works for self-audits and research with a defined authorization.

sections.heading: Start with a known reference
sections.body:
Write the claim you are checking before opening results, and use a reference controlled by that project such as its official website account-links page.

A search snippet, scraped directory, or another username checker is not an independent reference if it repeats the same source. For your own old account, saved signup emails and a recognized login provide private confirmation without publishing those records.

sections.heading: Check that the result is actually a profile
sections.body:
Open the exact candidate URL and verify the current handle, page type, and final destination. A platform may return a login page, generic application shell, or soft error with a successful HTTP status, so a username in the URL alone is never sufficient.

A user page can also redirect to an organization or a renamed account. In MyRecon, keep found, not found, and unknown distinct; a blocked or timed-out check cannot be promoted to confirmed.

sections.heading: Rank evidence by independence
sections.body:
An official website linking directly to an account is stronger evidence for a public association than a similar display name. Two profiles using the same avatar are not necessarily two independent clues because images are easily copied.

A reciprocal link can help, though compromised accounts can also publish misleading links. Record each source, explain why it is independent, and stop short of establishing legal identity.

sections.heading: Use a decision log rather than a numerical confidence score
sections.body:
Make columns for claim, candidate URL, observation, supporting source, conflicting evidence, and conclusion (candidate only, public association corroborated, conflicting evidence, or unable to verify). Do not turn an unvalidated percentage into evidence.

When details conflict, write the conflict directly: for example, the official project links to a different handle or the candidate advertises an unrelated organization. Absence of a backlink is not by itself a disproof.

sections.heading: Worked example: a reused handle
sections.body:
Illustrative case: a project website links to github.com/example-studio, while a social profile named example_studio uses a similar avatar with no project link. The GitHub association is supported by the project source, while the social profile stays a candidate.

Add a follow-up only if your research purpose requires it; do not infer a shared person, email address, or location. Record the observation date because links and handles can change.

sections.heading: Write a report another reviewer can challenge
sections.body:
Include the claim, original URLs, observation time, positive evidence, conflicts, and unavailable sources, and separate signed-out observations from authorized logins.

Leave irrelevant personal details out. If a page cannot be reproduced later, keep the dated observation rather than editing history; a defensible result may stay unresolved.

faq.question: Does the same avatar prove two accounts are linked?
faq.answer: No. Images can be copied. Look for independent, source-controlled links and record conflicts.

faq.question: What should I do with a blocked profile?
faq.answer: Record unable to verify, including the blocked source and date. Do not treat a block as proof of existence or absence.

faq.question: Can public links verify a legal identity?
faq.answer: They can support a public association. Legal identity and current account control require a separate verification process.

takeaways: Check that the result is actually a profile
method: Worked examples are illustrative unless explicitly labeled as observed. Product limits were checked against the release source; linked provider instructions describe external workflows, not a claim that every account flow was tested.
